newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails job performance of federal workers.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails job performance of federal workers.

text.p: President Clinton Thursday credited federal workers with helping to restore confidence in government, saying their job performance had caused a "stunning turnaround" in public opinion.

In a statement of praise for civil servants -- a group more accustomed to bureaucrat-bashing from politicians than congratulatory words -- Clinton said he was impressed with the performance of the federal workforce during his presidency.

"Four years ago, public confidence in the federal government was at all all-time low. But you have begun to change that attitude. Even in a time of leaner budgets and smaller staffs, you have improved service to the public, forged effective partnerships with communities and private businesses and discarded old-fashioned management systems," the Democratic president said.
"Now for the first time in decades, public opinion of federal agencies is markedly on the rise," Clinton said. "Congratulations -- the credit for this stunning turnaround goes to you."
Clinton has often boasted of his efforts to shrink the federal workforce, saying the federal payroll is now the smallest it has been since John Kennedy's presidency in the early 1960s.

And shortly before the White House put out the president's statement, Vice President Al Gore boasted at a budget briefing that the administration was "two years ahead of schedule in downsizing the government."
